zeolite-13x-humid.description: Zeolite 13X beads for humid gas, CO2/N2/H2O, competitive dual-site Langmuir; water fitted to the isotherms of Son, Richardson and Cmarik (J. Chem. Eng. Data 2019) below 60 % relative humidity (7 % RMS error)

references.citation: R. Haghpanah, A. Majumder, R. Nilam, A. Rajendran, S. Farooq, I. A. Karimi, M. Amanullah. Multiobjective optimization of a four-step adsorption process for postcombustion CO2 capture via finite volume simulation. Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 52 (2013) 4249-4265
K. N. Son, J. A. Richardson, G. E. Cmarik. Equilibrium adsorption isotherms for H2O on zeolite 13X. J. Chem. Eng. Data 64 (2019) 1063-1071

assumptions: water: competitive dual-site Langmuir fitted by SwingPy to the measured isotherms of Son et al. (Table 1) below 60 % relative humidity, 7 % RMS error, up to 19 % at the lowest pressures
heat of adsorption of water 65 kJ/mol, within the range of the fitted site energies

calf-20.description: CALF-20, structured (extrudates with polysulfone binder), CO2/N2, dual-site Langmuir with the equal energy scheme for N2

references.citation: T. T. T. Nguyen, G. K. H. Shimizu, A. Rajendran. CO2/N2 separation by vacuum swing adsorption using a metal-organic framework, CALF-20: Multi-objective optimization and experimental validation. Chem. Eng. J. 452 (2023) 139550 (values from Table 1 and Table A1 of the preprint, ChemRxiv 10.26434/chemrxiv-2022-c7hp1)

assumptions: particle radius 0.5 mm: the article gives no radius, only extrudates of 1 mm diameter and 1 to 3 mm length
heats of adsorption equal to the internal energies of the isotherm (site b for CO2)
heat capacity of the adsorbed phase equal to that of gaseous CO2 (841 J/(kg K)), as the article assumes
